title: The meeting before the deadline
intro: Learning goal: practise evidence-based, respectful disagreement under pressure. For individual or group use. Before each choice, note your instinct; after an outcome, compare it with another route.

nodes.title: Ten minutes before the review
nodes.body: You coordinate a small project team. Sam has found an accessibility barrier in the prototype. Alex says there is no time to change anything. Your role is to agree a credible next step without hiding the barrier.

nodes.title: How do you open the discussion?
nodes.body: Alex interrupts Sam: "We already agreed this design." The room goes quiet.
nodes.prompt: Write your first instinct before choosing.

choices.label: Make space for Sam to demonstrate the barrier
Take the disagreement out of the meeting

nodes.title: A barrier everyone can see
nodes.body: Sam shows that the keyboard cannot reach the final action. Alex acknowledges the problem but worries that a large change would break other screens.

nodes.title: What change will you propose?
nodes.body: The team can test a narrow fix today, or postpone this interaction and explain why.

choices.label: Try a narrow keyboard fix with a test
Remove the interaction from this release

nodes.title: The first test is promising
nodes.body: The final action is reachable. Sam asks to check focus visibility and the order of controls before declaring the whole interaction accessible.

nodes.title: What counts as ready?
nodes.body: You have time for one more focused check before the review.

choices.label: Run the check and describe the limits honestly
Call the interaction fully accessible now

nodes.title: A clear record
nodes.body: The focused check finds one confusing focus indicator. You fix it and record what was tested, what was not, and who will review next.

nodes.title: Lead the review
nodes.body: The reviewer asks why the design changed so late.

choices.label: Explain the barrier, fix, checks and remaining limits

nodes.title: A smaller release
nodes.body: The team can offer the same learning content as a straightforward reading activity. It loses the interaction but avoids publishing a known keyboard barrier.

nodes.title: Check the replacement
nodes.body: The replacement needs a clear purpose and a quick access check too.

choices.label: Test the replacement and record the deferred feature
Assume simple content needs no checking

nodes.title: The conversation becomes quieter
nodes.body: Alex is less defensive in private. Sam is no longer present to demonstrate the issue. You still need evidence, not a decision based only on who speaks most confidently.

nodes.title: Rebuild a shared view
nodes.body: How will you bring the concern back into the plan?

choices.label: Invite Sam to show the barrier with the whole team
Let Alex decide whether the concern matters

nodes.title: The original plan continues
nodes.body: The concern is treated as a preference rather than an access barrier. Sam sends a written example so it is not lost.

nodes.title: The written example arrives
nodes.body: The review has not begun. There is still time to make the issue visible.

choices.label: Return to the evidence and agree a limited response
Leave the issue out of the review

nodes.title: Outcome / a shared, evidence-led plan
nodes.body: The team can explain its decisions and remaining uncertainty. Sam and Alex both have clear next actions. Debrief: which choice helped the team disagree constructively?
nodes.prompt: What would you transfer to a real meeting?

nodes.title: Outcome / a deliberate smaller release
nodes.body: The team releases a checked alternative and names the deferred interaction. This is a different strategy, not an automatic failure. Debrief: what learning value was retained, and what was lost?
nodes.prompt: When would a smaller release be appropriate?

nodes.title: Outcome / confidence beyond the evidence
nodes.body: The review receives a stronger claim than the tests support. The next task is to correct that claim and agree further checks. Debrief: what would an honest description have said?
nodes.prompt: Rewrite the claim using only the evidence you have.

nodes.title: Outcome / an unresolved barrier
nodes.body: The plan goes forward without a clear check or visible record of the issue. A learner may still be blocked. Debrief: identify an earlier opportunity to change this route.
nodes.prompt: Which earlier decision would you revisit, and why?
